newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonian bourse has first insider dealing case.
newsitem.headline: Estonian bourse has first insider dealing case.

text.p: Estonia's fledgling stock market experienced its first investigation into alleged insider dealing on Wednesday, as shares in meat factory Rakvere were suspended pending a police investigation.
The securities commission said it has asked the police to initiate charges of illegal dealing in the company's shares.

"The reason was deals made by persons who possessed confidential information at a time when possession of the information could have an impact on the security's price," the securities commission said in a statement.

Just before trading closed on May 15, the Estonian firm informed the stock exchange that it had bought a majority stake in a leading meat producer in neighbouring Latvia, Rigas Miesnieks. Rakvere shares gained nearly 10 percent on May 14 and 15.

"The securities commission suspects that before the release of official information on the bourse and on news agencies the data was used in a price sensitive period for personal interests," said commission deputy director Indrek Jakobson.
"This is a precedent in Estonia which has an enormous impact for the Estonian market," he added.
The bourse, although tiny compared with other east European markets such as Poland, marked its first anniversary in May and is seen as the most liquid and successful in the Baltic region.
The stock exchange was not worried by the case and was pleased the securities commission was prepared to tackle tough issues.

"It will have a favourable impact and it shows that a state institution has brought the problem into consciousness and the problem is being dealt with," bourse managing director Helo Meigas told Reuters.
